question_text: Describe the full lifecycle of activity at the keynote hall on 2025-12-08 (UTC). Cover: (a) door entry patterns at KeynoteHall_DoorA throughout the day, (b) the in-hall crowd density at KeynoteHall_Stage during keynote sessions, and (c) how the post-keynote dispersal compares to pre-keynote build-up. Use specific hours and numbers from the data. 4-6 sentences.

rubric: KeynoteHall_DoorA shows entry peaks aligned with keynote start times (around 08:00-10:00, 13:00-14:00, or 15:00-16:00 UTC)
KeynoteHall_Stage crowd peaks during the keynote sessions, reaching head_counts in the hundreds
Outside of keynote hours the in-hall head_count drops to a low baseline (single digits)
Pre-keynote door entry traffic precedes the in-hall crowd surge

answer_text: On December 8, 2025, KeynoteHall_DoorA exhibited intense door entry activity, peaking with 411 entries between 15:00 and 16:00 UTC and a total of 2,209 events recorded throughout the day, which included 1,117 person entries. The density at KeynoteHall_Stage during key sessions showed an average head count of approximately 450.19 around 09:00 UTC, with a peak of 500, signifying a vibrant build-up of attendees prior to keynotes. In contrast, post-keynote dispersal recorded a significantly lower exit count of just 3, highlighting a dramatic drop in crowd density compared to the pre-keynote phase. This illustrates the stark difference in attendance dynamics surrounding key presentations and the subsequent dispersal of the crowd.
